text:
Love of Your Life!, good performance by Margaret Qualley but needed more emotional build-up.

I just completed watching Amazon's release Love of Your Life and wanted to put my thoughts up here.
 At the start, I felt like the story was going a little too fast. I think the writers should’ve made better decisions on showing scenes/moments, so we could feel more connected... at first, it just feels like a regular romantic drama.
 As it goes on, toward the end, you really start to feel for Maya’s character. She wasn't from a regular family, and after Charlie's death, she didn't want to face his family. She basically went ghost to handle her grief, turning to drinking and ONS just to cope. Then she meets Felix, which acts as a distraction from her pain. But when she sees his daughter, she realizes she doesn't want to ruin another family. Even after she decides to give herself one more chance with Felix, rejection of Felix give her push to finally overcome grief. The moment she confronts the friend and Charlie's mother at the end was good, though they didn't really give enough build-up to Charlie and Maya's relationship and her emotions more overall.
 I’ve been a fan of Margaret Qualley since MAID, and she did a great job as the lead here, she carries the film. By the end, it really hits you with lots of thoughts about Maya’s choices. If they had shown a few more emotional moments, it would have landed harder and been a much better film. 
 I’d give it a 6.3/10.
 Also want to here your thoughts on this!

Second, it seems like whenever there’s an object that is huge, a boulder, a building, a giant, that when it falls, it falls in slow motion. For some reason in movies, the bigger, the object, the slower it falls, when it would really fall just as quickly as any other object. There’s a ton of pet peeves but these are ones.
